## Question

How many mutations did *E. coli* accumulate over 50,000 generations of the
Long-Term Evolution Experiment [@tenaillon2016], and is that answer robust to
how strictly we filter the variant calls?

This report summarizes read quality, variant counts, and sensitivity to the minimum read depth used for filtering.

## Data

```{python}
#| tags: [parameters]
# Number of reads per file used for the length, GC and quality summaries.
# Change it without editing the report: quarto render ... -P max_reads:5000
max_reads = 10000
```

```{python}
#| label: setup
#| echo: false
import sys

import matplotlib
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import pandas as pd

from scripts.fastq_stats import quality_by_position, summarize

samples = pd.read_csv("metadata/samples.tsv", sep="\t", keep_default_na=False)
fastq_files = list(samples["fastq_1"]) + list(samples["fastq_2"])
```

We use a subset of the reads prepared by Data Carpentry [@dc_data]: three
clones of population Ara-3, frozen at generations
`{python} ", ".join(f"{g:,}" for g in samples["generation"])`
(@tbl-samples).

```{python}
#| label: tbl-samples
#| tbl-cap: "The three LTEE clones in this project."
samples[["sample", "strain", "generation", "mutator", "cit"]]
```

## Reads

```{python}
#| label: tbl-reads
#| tbl-cap: "Reads per FASTQ file. Length, GC content and mean base quality are computed on the first reads of each file (parameter `max_reads`)."
reads = pd.DataFrame([summarize(f, max_reads) for f in sorted(fastq_files)])
reads.round(1)
```

Each file has `{python} f"{reads['reads'].min():,}"` reads, so each sample has
`{python} f"{reads['reads'].min():,}"` read pairs. The mean read length is
`{python} f"{reads['mean_length'].mean():.0f}"` bases because the reads were
trimmed before subsampling. @fig-quality shows that base quality stays high
along the reads.

```{python}
#| label: fig-quality
#| fig-cap: "Mean base quality along the reads (first `max_reads` reads of each file). Colour shows the sample, line style the read of the pair."
#| fig-alt: "Line plot of mean Phred quality against position in the read, six lines (three samples, read 1 solid and read 2 dashed). Quality starts near 32, peaks near 39 around position 15, falls to about 33 by position 80 and stays there to position 150, with a brief dip near position 102. All six files follow the same shape."
colors = ["#2a78d6", "#eb6834", "#1baf7a"]  # one per sample, in generation order
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 4.2))
for color, (_, row) in zip(colors, samples.sort_values("generation").iterrows()):
    for read, style in [("fastq_1", "-"), ("fastq_2", "--")]:
        quality_by_position(row[read], max_reads).plot(
            ax=ax, color=color, linestyle=style, linewidth=1.5,
            label=f"{row['sample']} (gen. {row['generation']:,}) read {read[-1]}")
ax.set_xlabel("Position in read (bases)")
ax.set_ylabel("Mean Phred quality")
ax.grid(alpha=0.3)
ax.legend(fontsize=7, ncol=3, frameon=False, loc="upper center", bbox_to_anchor=(0.5, -0.18))
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

The mean GC content is `{python} f"{reads['gc_percent'].mean():.1f}"`%.

## Variants

Reads are aligned to REL606 with BWA, followed by variant calling with
bcftools and filtering with `vcfutils.pl varFilter`. The Snakemake workflow
reads its settings from `config/config.yaml`. The
[MultiQC report](../results/qc/multiqc/multiqc_report.html) summarizes read QC.

```{python}
#| label: setup-variants
from pathlib import Path
import yaml

with open("config/config.yaml") as fh:
    config = yaml.safe_load(fh)

def count_variants(path):
    with open(path) as fh:
        return sum(1 for line in fh if not line.startswith("#"))

variants = samples[["sample", "generation", "mutator"]].sort_values("generation").copy()
variants["variants"] = [count_variants(f"results/vcf/{s}_final_variants.vcf") for s in variants["sample"]]
```

```{python}
#| label: tbl-variants
#| tbl-cap: "Variant records per clone at the configured minimum depth."
variants
```

These counts describe variant calls from the subsampled reads, rather than
an exhaustive inventory of mutations in each genome. The late clone is
annotated as a mutator in the sample metadata.

### Sensitivity to read depth

```{python}
#| label: fig-sensitivity
#| fig-cap: "Variant counts at each minimum depth, plotted by generation."
#| fig-alt: "Line plot comparing variant counts across generations for each configured minimum read depth."
sens = pd.DataFrame([
    {"sample": row["sample"], "generation": row["generation"], "depth": depth,
     "variants": count_variants(f"results/sensitivity/{row['sample']}_d{depth}.vcf")}
    for _, row in variants.iterrows()
    for depth in config["sensitivity_depths"]
])
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 4.2))
for depth, group in sens.groupby("depth"):
    group = group.sort_values("generation")
    ax.plot(group["generation"], group["variants"], marker="o", label=f"Minimum depth {depth}")
ax.set_yscale("symlog", linthresh=1)
ax.set_xlabel("Generation")
ax.set_ylabel("Variant records (log scale above 1)")
ax.set_xticks(variants["generation"], [f"{g:,}" for g in variants["generation"]])
ax.grid(alpha=0.3)
ax.legend(frameon=False)
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

```{python}
#| label: tbl-sensitivity
#| tbl-cap: "Variant counts by sample and minimum depth."
sensitivity_table = sens.pivot(index=["generation", "sample"], columns="depth", values="variants").sort_index()
sensitivity_table
```

**Decision.** We retain minimum depth `{python} config["min_depth"]` for the
main result to preserve comparability with the original shell workflow,
and present all tested thresholds so the effect of filtering remains visible.
For the tested thresholds, the table and figure show whether the ordering
of clones persists and how strongly the absolute counts change.

These three clones and subsampled reads alone do not establish a population-wide
mutation rate. See `docs/decisions.md` for the analysis decision.
